cim: Missouri S&T aims for AI undergrad degree next fall
cim_eredeti: Missouri S&T aims for AI undergrad degree next fall
szoveg_eredeti:
ROLLA, Mo.— Missouri S&T University is one step closer to establishing the state’s first standalone undergraduate degree for artificial intelligence.

University of Missouri System’s Board of Curators unanimously approved the bachelor’s degree proposal on Thursday. The 120-credit hour program would be within the Missouri S&T’s computer science department, in the College of Engineering and Computing.

“Demand for AI-focused education has grown significantly as AI technologies become increasingly integrated into industries ranging from manufacturing and transportation to healthcare and financial services,” says Dr. David Borrok, vice provost and dean of the College of Engineering and Computing at S&T. “Our graduates will be prepared to understand and innovate within modern engineered systems that are increasingly using AI.”

Pending approval by the Missouri Coordinating Board for Higher Education, the AI degree could enroll student next Fall and they expect to have 110 enrollees within five years.

Six new courses were specifically developed for the program’s curriculum: Introduction to Modern AI Tools, Introduction to Artificial Intelligence, Introduction to Machine Learning, Intelligent Robots, Responsible AI and Computer, and an AI Capstone course. Enrollees will go through hands-on learning experiences involving AI.

“Experiential learning will be a key component of this program,” says Dr. Seung-Jong Jay Park, S&T’s Kummer Endowed Chair of Computer Science. “Students will complete project-based coursework and participate in a senior capstone experience that may be sponsored by industry, government laboratories or university researchers.”

These will cover core topics of programming, algorithms, machine learning, computer organization, data science, databases and cybersecurity. Students will learn coursework in calculus, linear algebra, statistics and neuroscience.

Missouri S&T says the degree aligns with the university’s strategic goals of enrollment growth, academic innovation and workforce preparation. It also comes after Gov. Mike Kehoe’s Executive Order that directed higher education and businesses to support the development of AI-focused degree programs.

“Graduates will prepare for careers such as AI application developer, machine learning engineer, data scientist, intelligent systems developer, AI solutions analyst and AI-enabled cybersecurity analyst,” stated a Missouri S&T spokesperson.
